title: A common multiplier for local ideal generators
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I,p$ ideals with $p$ prime, $e\geq0$, and $h_1,\ldots,h_e\in R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] generating $IR_p$. Then there exist $F_1,\ldots,F_e\in I$ and $A\in R\setminus p$ such that $Ax\in(F_1,\ldots,F_e)$ for every $x\in I$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), proof of (2) implies (1), paragraph beginning with clearing the denominators d_i; source checked online and algebra.tex read in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: Membership of each h_i in the extended ideal gives F_i in I and s_i outside p with h_i times s_i/1 = F_i/1, by IsLocalization.mem_map_algebraMap_iff. Set J=(F_i). Since s_i/1 is a unit, Ideal.unit_mul_mem_iff_mem shows h_i lies in JR_p. Thus IR_p is contained in JR_p.

Choose a finite generating set t of I by isNoetherianRing_iff_ideal_fg. For each x in t, its image lies in JR_p. IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff gives v_x outside p with v_x*x in J. Set A to the product of these v_x.

The prime complement is multiplicatively closed, so A is outside p. Each v_x divides A, giving A*x in J for x in t. Submodule.span_induction extends this membership to all of I: multiplication by A preserves zero and sums, and commutes with scalar multiplication. For t empty, A=1.

mathlib_searches.query: A finite family generating an ideal localized at a prime can be cleared to global ideal elements with one common denominator outside the prime
A finitely generated ideal generated by e elements at a prime is generated by e elements after inverting one element outside the prime
mathlib_searches.results: Ideal.fg_of_localizationSpan and module finite-localization results; no theorem supplying the fixed e numerators and common multiplier.
Ideal.map_span and singleton-span results, no common multiplier theorem.
Localization/Ideal.lean lines 55 and 76 and Ideal/Defs.lean line 75 give precisely the fraction-membership and unit-cancellation tools used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_clearing_of_local_generators
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (e : ℕ) (h : Fin e → Localization.AtPrime p)
    (hgen : Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) I =
      Ideal.span (Set.range h)) :
    ∃ (F : Fin e → R) (A : R), A ∉ p ∧ (∀ i, F i ∈ I) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ I, A * x ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range F)
